text:
Maya Patel: Hey folks — I'm the new on-call shadow next week (Mon-Wed). Wanted to confirm primary/secondary pairing and run through a quick checklist. Who's comfortable being primary while I shadow?

Sam Ortiz: I can be primary Mon/Tue morning, then Alex takes over Tue afternoon -> Wed.

Alex Chen: Yup, happy to take Tue PM + Wed. Maya, you'll shadow me on the escalation path and postmortem steps.

Maya Patel: Awesome, thanks. Can someone post the quick runbook links and any non-obvious pager noise to ignore?

Katie Nguyen: Quick pointers:
- Runbooks: https://redwood.example/runbooks/oncall (follow the "incident triage" section)
- SLO dashboard: https://dash.redwood.example/slo
- Escalation matrix: https://redwood.example/escalation (pages to oncall->eng-sre->eng-lead)

Liam O'Connor: Also note the noisy alert that triggers on infra-restarts in eu-west (reduce attention unless customers impacted). Runbook has the filter snippet.

Oncall Bot: Scheduled paging test will run at 2026-03-20T15:00:00Z. Paging workflow: primary gets SMS + push, secondary receives Slack DM fallback after 2m if not acknowledged. Reaction ":white_check_mark:" to confirm you saw this message.

Sam Ortiz: Confirming schedule:
```
Mon: Sam (primary), Alex (secondary), Maya (shadow Sam)
Tue AM: Sam (primary), Tue PM: Alex (primary), Maya (shadow both)
Wed: Alex (primary), Sam (secondary), Maya (shadow Alex)
```

Maya Patel: Thanks. A few onboarding asks: 1) Can we run through a live mock page during shadowing? 2) How do I access the incident logging template?

Alex Chen: Yes to mock page. We'll trigger a low-risk alert (non-customer-facing) and walk through the steps: acknowledge, create incident doc, run triage checks, and handoff notes. Incident template: https://redwood.example/templates/incident (look for "oncall-shadowing" variant).

Katie Nguyen: For access: request access to the incident-docs Google folder and to PagerDuty; we've added Maya to the request queue but ping me if it's not approved by EOD.

Maya Patel: Got it. For the mock page, what's the easiest play to trigger? I don't want to accidentally cause any cascading jobs.

Sam Ortiz: Use the staging deploy-bot endpoint: POST https://staging.redwood.example/test-alert with body `{ "type": "oncall-shadow", "severity": "low" }`. It creates a synthetic alert that follows the normal paging path but excludes external webhooks.

Liam O'Connor: When you do the mock, run through the checklist in the runbook. Two things to highlight: 1) checking prefix cache health (common root cause lately), 2) checking model-variant fallback logs (sometimes triggers cascade).

Oncall Bot: Reminder: if an active incident escalates to P1, secondary will be paged directly. Ensure rotations are up-to-date: https://oncall.redwood.example/rotations

Maya Patel: Can we add one more shadowing slot on Thu morning in case approvals are delayed?

Alex Chen: I can swap Wed->Thu if needed. Sam OK with Tue AM -> Thu AM shuffle?

Sam Ortiz: I can do Tue AM -> Thu AM instead, no problem.

Katie Nguyen: I'll approve access request now. Also dropping a short checklist in the chat for today:
- Verify PagerDuty login
- Confirm incident-docs write access
- Run the staging mock alert
- Walk through triage -> handoff -> postmortem draft

Maya Patel: Thanks Katie, will watch for access and run mock once it's cleared. One last ask: any common gotchas you wish you knew as a new shadow?

Alex Chen: A few quick ones: 
- Don't rely on the console's timestamps for ordering; use the incident doc chronology.
- If you see repeated "gateway-timeout" across regions, check the smart-routing fallback first.
- For customer-impact check, we always check the last 1000 tokens served in the last 5m in the SLO dashboard (it's quick).

Sam Ortiz: Also, it's ok to escalate early. If you think multiple downstream services are failing, page SRE earlier rather than later.

Maya Patel: Great, thanks everyone. I'll post here once access is confirmed and schedule the mock alert. :thumbsup:

Oncall Bot: Paging test result: SUCCESS (2026-03-20T15:00:10Z). Sam acknowledged in 25s.

Alex Chen: Nice. Maya — when you're ready we can do the mock.

Maya Patel: Access is live. I'll trigger the mock at 2026-03-21T17:00Z and invite Alex to join.

Katie Nguyen: I'll watch for the incident doc and help with the postmortem template.

Sam Ortiz: Thanks team. Welcome onboard, Maya! :party_parrot:
